messages:
Jess: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector change from yesterday I'm seeing a new perf regression in paged-attn. 99p latency for some L0 workloads jumped ~15-25% and GPU utilisation has these weird sawtooth spikes.
Omar: saw something similar on a prod replica. Looks correlated with high cache churn + large batch tails. Can you paste traces? :thinking:
Jess: pasted a short profile from the run:
```
# perf summary (nvprof-like) for batch=32, seq=2048
flash_variant_a: mean token ms 0.82, p99 1.9
paged_attn_v2 (kernel-route B): mean token ms 0.95, p99 2.3
kv-page-evict ops spikes at 1.2k/s during regress window
GPU mem alloc/free churn ~600 ops/s
```
Omar: kv-page-evict ops that high is the smell. Our block-table freelist is doing a lot of small allocs which pushes the kernel choice to non-fused paths.
Liam: I profiled trace events and saw frequent small slab splits + compaction kicks — compaction runs on free threshold, which is being tripped by rapid page evictions from the prefix cache.
Rachael: summary from PerfBot: :robot_face: "regression detected — paged_attn: p99 latency +18% vs baseline; increased memory allocator syscalls; kernel selection flip events up by 3.6x"
PerfBot: attached flamegraph link: https://perf.redwood/internal/fg/3632104444 (private)
Jess: hypothesis — the kernel-selector now favors a lower-latency fused path only when contiguous KV blocks are present. The fallback to flash-variant A when blocks are fragmented causes higher p99. But fragmentation is driven by the current freelist strategy which splits into tiny chunks on evict.
Omar: proposed mitigation in short: try a "nursery-allocator" for recently-created KV pages (generational approach). Keep small hot pages in a compact slab so kernel-selector sees contiguous runs. Evict from old generation first.
Liam: +1. Implementation notes I sketched: maintain two arenas per block-table shard: nursery (compact, append-only until full) and main (free-lists, chunked). On eviction, promote or demote based on access-age. Compaction only runs on main and at coarser intervals.
Rachael: any thoughts on batcher heuristics? If batching creates long tail batches with mixed contiguous/non-contiguous keys, kernel-selector might oscillate mid-request. Could we annotate batches with contiguous-run score so runtime chooses a single kernel for the whole batch?
Jess: yeah we can compute a simple heuristic: contiguous-run-percent = contiguous_tokens / total_tokens. If > 0.85 use fused path, else use paged path. Cheap to compute from KV layout metadata.
Omar: experiments I'd run: 1) enable nursery allocator (local) 2) add contiguous-run score gating in kernel-selector 3) instrument kernel-flip counter and per-batch contiguous metric. Measure p50/p95/p99 and KV-evict ops.
Liam: rough microbench plan: synthetic mix that interleaves long context chat (high prefix reuse) + many short queries (causes eviction). Run with and without nursery, and with/without gating. Collect traces with `./tools/trace-collector --batcher --kernel-decisions`.
Jess: quick config snippet for the gating:
```
kernel_selector:
  contiguous_threshold: 0.85
  min_tokens_for_fused: 256
  fallback: flash_variant_a
```
Omar: one more thought — adjust freelist allocation to prefer coalescing when evict size < page_size/4. That reduces fragmentation from small evicts. But risk: higher latency on single large free/alloc ops. Need bench.
Rachael: agree. Also add telemetry: percent of batches that flip kernel mid-stream. Right now we only log kernel per-request, not per-batch-stage.
PerfBot: automation suggestion: run A/B on a sample dedicated pool using the config flag `runtime.paged_attn.nursery=true` and `runtime.selector.gate_contiguous=true`. Collect 24h windows and compare unit cost & p99.
Jess: next steps — Omar/Liam pair to prototype nursery allocator + freelist tweak, Rachael to wire contiguous-run telemetry into batcher, I'll run initial A/B after we have a smoke build. Targeting an experiment by EOD+2.
Omar: I'll start a branch `nursery-paged-attn` and post WIP in this thread.
Liam: I'll add microbench harness and a set of small scripts to diff kernel decisions.
Rachael: I'll add telemetry PR to batcher (small change) and a dashboard template.
Jess: thanks — keeping this thread to track perf regress triage. Please ping if you hit blockers. :thumbsup:
